categories.name: Stacked segment position vs. length
categories.definition: Reads a stacked bar/area segment's value from its cumulative boundary position, the stack total, or an off-baseline comparison instead of decoding the segment's own length or thickness.

categories.name: Truncated or distorted scale taken at face value
categories.definition: Judges magnitudes or ratios from drawn lengths/slopes as if the scale were linear and zero-based, when the axis is truncated, non-linear, compressed, or inconsistent across panels.

categories.name: Default convention overrides actual encoding
categories.definition: Applies conventional encoding assumptions (up means more, left-to-right is time, darker/larger means more) without checking axis directions, label order, or legend mappings that are inverted or scrambled.

categories.name: Series/legend mapping error
categories.definition: Associates the wrong series, line, segment, slice, column, or map region with the queried category due to legend-color confusion, similar hues, label-to-mark mismatches, or tracking a salient wrong series.

categories.name: Adjacent or wrong element lookup
categories.definition: Locates the wrong data element (neighboring point, bar, bin, row, sector, or year) when aligning labels, ticks, or coordinates with marks, and reads its value instead of the queried one.

categories.name: Wrong axis or encoding channel
categories.definition: Reads the queried variable from the wrong axis or visual channel, e.g., using vertical position when the variable is on the x-axis or encoded by mark size.

categories.name: Level vs. change confusion
categories.definition: Confuses a value's level with its change: reads the highest line as the biggest increase, reports an endpoint instead of a difference, or swaps absolute and relative change.

categories.name: Average substituted or biased
categories.definition: Answers average questions with a midrange, mode, maximum, single salient value, or an estimate dominated by a subset of the data instead of integrating all values.

categories.name: Incomplete extremum search
categories.definition: Finds maxima/minima/outliers/top-N by incomplete or satisficing scanning: stops at a local, salient, or first-encountered candidate instead of exhaustively comparing all data.

categories.name: Range misconstrued
categories.definition: Reports a range or extreme using axis limits, first-to-last values, or the bulk of the data instead of the actual minimum and maximum of the plotted values.

categories.name: Question term misinterpreted
categories.definition: Misparses the question's wording or a statistical concept: 'lowest peak' as trough, 'biggest difference' as biggest bars, reversed comparison direction, decreasing vs. low, outlier or correlation sign misunderstood.

categories.name: Multi-condition filter misapplied
categories.definition: In compound queries, applies only one condition, uses too loose or too strict a tolerance for terms like 'high' or 'approximately the same', or filters/ranks on the wrong variable.

categories.name: Trend judged from wrong scope
categories.definition: Judges a trend or universal claim from a subrange, salient segment, endpoints, or pooled data instead of the specified interval, every data point, or the correct subgroup; includes demanding monotonicity or extrapolating beyond the plotted range.

categories.name: Prior knowledge over data
categories.definition: Answers from real-world expectations or familiarity with the labels rather than from the values actually displayed.

categories.name: Partial data treated as final
categories.definition: Compares an incomplete current-period value against complete periods or treats in-progress counts as a settled outcome, ignoring stated incompleteness.

categories.name: Decodable chart deemed unanswerable
categories.definition: Declares that a readable, fully specified chart cannot answer the question—often after detecting an unconventional or deceptive design—instead of decoding it from its labels.

categories.name: Labels, annotations, and encoding limits mishandled
categories.definition: Mishandles the relationship between printed information and encoded data: trusts annotations or labels without verification (or trusts distorted visuals over labels), ignores that bins hide variation, misses denominators, or treats a sample/trend line as deterministic truth.

categories.name: Perceptual precision limits
categories.definition: Errors from limited visual resolution: imprecise interpolation between gridlines, snapping to ticks, misjudged angles/areas/radial distances, indiscriminable color shades, or overlapping marks merged together.

categories.name: Counting and tally slips
categories.definition: Loses count or misses items when tallying marks: overlooks tiny or edge-of-plot marks, drops a row of icons, or makes row-matching slips in tables.

categories.name: Threshold comparison errors
categories.definition: Errs when comparing values to a cutoff: treats strict inequalities as inclusive, miscounts near-threshold cases that are visually hard to resolve, or mislocates where a series crosses a threshold.

categories.name: Wrong quantity computed
categories.definition: Computes a different quantity than asked: wrong denominator or part-to-remainder ratios, a single value instead of a difference, flow confused with cumulative total, or the wrong subset aggregated.

categories.name: No systematic misconception
categories.definition: The response pattern is consistent with guessing, inattention, or hedging rather than any identifiable systematic misreading.
